B.narration:
You take out the lighter.

“4192”

That wasn't there when you put it in your pocket. The hand that cut it isn't yours.

The air tastes of metallic dust and deep, heavy silence presses against your ears.

You locked the door. Somewhere, you didn't.

prompt.content: You add one sentence of atmosphere to a quiet, literary horror story, in second person, present tense. Concrete senses only: sound, cold, light, smell, touch. No dialogue.

Where you are: your apartment. With you: no one. The power is out; the only light is the storm's. Something impossible has just happened, and you have gone very still.
Write ONE short sentence (under 20 words) about what you sense around you. No names, no numbers, no quotes, no words in ALL CAPS, and don't explain anything. Nothing about your body, skin, hands or feet, and nothing about shoes. Never use these words: ozone, wet stone, damp stone, bare feet, skin, chill, viscous.

D.narration:
Something small and heavy clicks against the floor by your feet. A brass key on a paper tag that says BASEMENT 07. Nobody threw it.

“WAIT”

You've never seen this key before. Yet someone has written on its tag. It's your handwriting. You don't remember writing it.

A low rumble vibrates through the solid expanse beneath you.

You trusted Teo. Somewhere, you followed her down.

Where you are: the roof, outdoors. It is raining hard. With you: no one. The power is out; the only light is the storm's. Something impossible has just happened, and you have gone very still.
Write ONE short sentence (under 20 words) about what you sense around you. No names, no numbers, no quotes, no words in ALL CAPS, and don't explain anything. Nothing about your body, skin, hands or feet, and nothing about shoes. Never use these words: ozone, wet stone, damp stone, bare feet, skin, chill, viscous.
Do not repeat the last one, or its images: The air tastes of metallic dust and deep, heavy silence presses against your ears.

ending.text:
You open the door.

They don't come in at once. They look past you, at the night you kept, the way you'd look at a room you used to live in.

You look down at what the night left you. "4192" scratched into the lighter, by Mara's hand. "WAIT" on the key's paper tag, in your own handwriting. Both made in a night you never lived.

One of them is in your handwriting. Now you know whose.

Teo was right. Up was just weather. The worst of it was always going to be at your own door.

In 6D, Teo's chain slides back. He opens his door to the empty hall and listens, and whatever he hears, he isn't afraid of it. "Finally," he says.

They step inside. You step back. There are two of you in the doorway, and the door won't close until one of you leaves.
changed: The brass key is at your feet. And it is in your hand. You can feel both, like holding one thing in two hands.
Your lighter is in your hand. It always was.
Mara is in the basement. She is also beside you; you can hear her, and she can hear herself. She doesn't look surprised.
